scenario: [LFAC.9.2]: the engine fills `ts` before it evaluates any of an emit's slot values, so where the wall clock has no value ([LTIM.2.8.3]) the fault recorded is the `ts` fill's ComputationError of kind DOMAIN, whatever a slot value would have raised. `Out` declares `ts`, and each of three rules emits an `Out` whose `q` is `t.a // t.b`, an Int floor division that traps DIVIDE_BY_ZERO when `b` is 0 ([LEXP.7.15.1]). Each rule takes one `Trig` by its key, so each fault is at its own (node, rule) site and none is latched away ([LERR.9.5]). The engine is on the mock clock and the wall clock starts with no value (`wall_clock: unset`). Step 1: `both` meets `b` = 0 with no wall clock, and both faults are possible; the fill's comes first, so `both DOMAIN`. Step 2, a control: `ts_only` meets `b` = 1 with no wall clock, so `ts_only DOMAIN`, and the fill's fault is reachable without a slot fault. Step 3, a control: the wall clock is set, and `trap_only` meets `b` = 0, so `trap_only DIVIDE_BY_ZERO`, and the slot's fault is reachable once the fill succeeds. `faulted` logs each ComputationError's rule and kind ([LERR.9.2]); `leaked` logs any `Out` in working memory and must never fire, because every emit here faults. Expected: `both DOMAIN`, `ts_only DOMAIN`, `trap_only DIVIDE_BY_ZERO`. A runtime that evaluates the slot values first logs `both DIVIDE_BY_ZERO` at step 1. PATH PINNED: libds `rete/engine.c`'s action loop, whose `ts_ix` fill (`ds_rete_eval_wall_ns` failing, DS_FAULT_DOMAIN) precedes its assigns; the Mercury runtime's `ds.exec.assert_verb`, whose `has_ts_slot` with `xc_wall = no` (`rf_domain`) precedes `assign_fault`.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope logical:
    k: Int key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable

schema Out scope logical:
    k: Int key
    q: Int mutable
    ts: Time

rule both:
    Trig t where t.k == 1
->
    emit Out logical k: t.k
        q: t.a // t.b

rule ts_only:
    Trig t where t.k == 2
->
    emit Out logical k: t.k
        q: t.a // t.b

rule trap_only:
    Trig t where t.k == 3
->
    emit Out logical k: t.k
        q: t.a // t.b

rule faulted:
    ComputationError c
->
    log info "{c.rule} {c.kind}"

rule leaked:
    Out
->
    log info "leaked"
